$comment: Findings we have consciously accepted, so they stop appearing as new every week.
This is not a suppression list — it is a decision log. Every entry carries a reason
and an expiry date, and once the expiry passes the finding resurfaces at full
severity. That is deliberate: an accepted risk that nobody re-examines for a year
is indistinguishable from a forgotten one.
id       — from security/finding-id.sh, stable across runs
reason   — why this is acceptable, in enough detail to re-judge it later

accepted.title: nginx forwards the client Host header upstream (proxy_set_header Host $host)
accepted.reason: Semgrep's generic.nginx.security.request-host-used fires on all four occurrences across portlog.conf and portlog.conf.http-only. Host header injection only becomes exploitable when the application derives absolute URLs from the request Host — password-reset links, redirects, canonical URLs in generated documents. Verified none exist: nothing in backend/src reads req.headers.host or request.host, and APP_URL is supplied by configuration rather than inferred. Accepted rather than fixed because setting a literal Host would need updating on every domain change, and the current form is correct for a single-vhost deployment. Re-check the moment any feature emails a link.
